programme: IRF3 and IRF9 sit in the same interferon-sensing relay: IRF3 is the transcription factor activated downstream of cGAS-STING/RIG-I sensing of nucleic acid, and IRF9 is the DNA-binding subunit of ISGF3 (with STAT1/STAT2) that executes the type-I-interferon transcriptional response. Their target lists overlap directly (IFIT1, CXCL8, TNFSF10, IL12A, CCL19), consistent with both factors converging on the same interferon-stimulated-gene (ISG) module rather than acting as unrelated hits.
role_in_a: In COPD airway epithelium, this axis is engaged by viral/dsRNA exposure: IRF3 drives an antiviral but hyperinflammatory response with PD-L1 induction, and IRF9 is epigenetically dysregulated to sustain excessive interferon signaling, contributing to chronic airway inflammation and exacerbation-prone epithelium.
role_in_b: In rectal/colorectal tumors, IRF3-linked cGAS-STING signaling couples innate immune sensing to tumor immune surveillance and to iron-dependent (ferroptotic) cell death, and IRF-family activity more broadly shapes the tumor immune infiltrate and prognosis, with TNFSF10 (TRAIL) among the shared downstream targets relevant to tumor cell death.
shared_axis: Chronic epithelial insult — cigarette smoke and recurrent viral infection in the airway, genotoxic/microbial stress in the colorectal mucosa — recruits the same cGAS-STING/RIG-I to IRF3 to type-I-IFN to ISGF3(IRF9) relay, producing an overlapping ISG/chemokine signature that in the lung sustains chronic inflammation and in the tumor shapes immune surveillance versus evasion (PD-L1, TRAIL).
reasoning: IRF9 is specifically and mechanistically placed in COPD (epigenetic dysregulation driving excess IFN signaling) and IRF3 is placed in both diseases via distinct papers (airway dsRNA/PD-L1 in COPD; cGAS-STING/ferroptosis and IRF-family tumor immunity in colorectal cancer), giving the module real anchoring in the record. But no retrieved source connects COPD and rectal cancer through this axis jointly, and the concordance rate (~38-41% of comparisons) is well below the top-recurring factor overall, so the cross-disease link is reasoned rather than retrieved.
support: PMID 41731077 — IRF9 epigenetic dysregulation drives excessive interferon signaling in COPD; PMID 39024368 — in-silico common molecular signatures between SARS-CoV-2 and lung disease implicating IRF9-linked signaling; PMID 42471816 — dsRNA drives hyperinflammatory, blunted antiviral response with PD-L1 induction via IRF3 pathway in COPD; PMID 38309095 — terpene treatment attenuates airway inflammation/obstruction (IRF3-adjacent, COPD); PMID 41869015 — cGAS-STING innate immunity linked to iron-dependent cell death in colorectal cancer context; PMID 34488791 — IRF family influences tumor immunity and prognosis in colorectal cancer patients.
how_to_falsify: Profile the shared ISG signature (IFIT1, CXCL8, TNFSF10, IL12A, CCL19) by RNA-seq or single-cell RNA-seq in matched COPD airway epithelium and rectal tumor epithelium, then perturb IRF3 (or upstream cGAS-STING) and IRF9 by knockdown/knockout in organoid or cell-line models of each tissue; if the same ISG module fails to move concordantly with IRF3/IRF9 perturbation in both tissues — or if IRF9 ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN in colorectal tumor cells shows no binding at these shared targets — the proposed shared axis is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is colorectal|lung across 260 patient-group comparisons from 6 independent cohort pairs. IRF3/IRF9 concordance (~38-41%) is notably lower than the highest-recurring factor in this list (IKZF2, 53%), which has no documented mechanism in either disease — recurrence and mechanistic support diverge here, so the account leans on the less-recurrent but better-evidenced pair. No explicit tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair, so the absence of a lung/colon master-regulator claim reflects the record given, not a filtered-out factor. SATB2 has by far the strongest single-disease record (multiple colorectal-cancer papers) but its target set is an EMT/Wnt/stemness programme (SNAI1/2, ZEB1, CDH1/2, AXIN2, LEF1, CD44, PROM1, NANOG) that does not overlap with IRF3/IRF9 targets, and its COPD evidence is a single genetic-association paper — it is treated as a separate, unconnected finding, not folded into this programme. ETV3 and HOXA1 are flagged discordant in the input (their target-set agreement did not actually hold across the two diseases) and are excluded from carrying_factors despite appearing in the list. Roughly half the listed factors (PIAS2, PATZ1, ZNF236, ZIC1, IKZF2) have no disease-specific evidence in either disease and are excluded from the account entirely.
